title: BTP services map: what lives where
summary: A beginner map of major BTP capability areas: app dev, integration, automation, data, AI, identity, ops.
explain:
Once you know BTP exists and how accounts work, learn the capability map (names evolve; categories stay useful):

• Application development — CAP, HTML5/Fiori, mobile, ABAP environment / RAP patterns for extensions.
• Integration — Integration Suite (iFlows, APIs, events, B2B).
• Automation — Build Process Automation (workflows, forms, rules).
• Data & analytics — HANA Cloud, Datasphere, Analytics Cloud, data product thinking.
• AI — grounded assistants, RAG patterns, responsible use (product names change).
• Identity & security — IAS/IPS concepts, XSUAA/roles, destinations, principal propagation.
• Operations — observability, entitlements, FinOps, SRE practices.

You do not need every service. You need the category that fits the business capability, then the simplest service that meets constraints.
analogy: A city map: not every trip uses the airport. Learn districts first (integration district, data district), then pick a street.
whyItMatters: Without a map, teams pick familiar tools for every problem and create accidental complexity.
formalPoints: Map business capability → platform category → service
Integration ≠ app dev ≠ data warehouse — different constraints
Identity and destinations cut across almost every design
Prefer fewer services with clear ownership
commonMistakes: Using CPI for pure UI apps or CAP for heavy B2B EDI without reason
Duplicating the same capability in three services
howToRecognize: Architecture workshops, portfolio rationalization, first landscape design
howToApply: For each initiative, write: capability, category, candidate service, rejected alternatives
